subject: Optimize toolkit — packaging, quantization & credits
messages:
From: Helen Carter <helen.carter@acmeretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Liu <alex.liu@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Optimize toolkit — packaging, quantization & credits

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Optimize recommendations engine looks promising. A few follow-ups from our infra and procurement teams so we can model the economics for a production rollout: 

1) Can you send a simple pricing / packaging breakdown for the Optimize toolkit (credits, per-token impacts after caching/batching, and recommended quantization paths)?
2) Do you offer committed-volume discounts or term-based pricing for banks of inference that leverage both batching and quantization guidance? If so, what are typical bands?
3) On the technical side, can you confirm engineering guidance: if we adopt your default batching + prefix cache recommendations and move to int8 quantization, what ballpark percentage savings should we expect vs our current float model runs? Any notes on when int4 is recommended?

Context: Acme Retail pilot will target ~6M tokens/month initially, mostly short sequences (~32 tokens for recalc + 128 tokens for session). Latency SLO is 150ms p95. We're already testing quantized variants in-house but want Redwood's recommendations and a commercial path (credits / discounts) that maps to our procurement cycle.

Procurement timeline: we need a one-page summary for internal approvers and a short MAP (mutual action plan) with milestones — hoping to close terms in July.

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Carter
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Retail
helen.carter@acmeretail.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Helen Carter <helen.carter@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Alex Liu <alex.liu@acmeretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — packaging, quantization & credits

Hi Helen — great to hear from you and glad the demo resonated. I put together a compact set of options tailored to your footprint and constraints; attaching a small spreadsheet with scenario-level math (attached). Key points below so procurement/infra has something concise to circulate.

Summary (short):
- Packaging: Optimize is sold as an add-on credit bundle that layers on top of token usage. We recommend starting with a Pilot bundle and migrating to a Commit bundle once usage stabilizes.
- Technical guidance: batching + prefix/KV caching usually yields 20–35% token-equivalent savings on typical recommendation workloads; int8 quantization adds ~25–35% per-token compute reduction versus float; int4 can add another ~10–18% but may require an eval pass for quality trade-offs on long-context generators.

Recommended commercial structures (example bands):
- Pilot — up to 3M tokens/month: one-off bundle = 300k Optimize credits (includes 1 workshop + baseline config) — list price $11,500
- Growth — 3–10M tokens/month: monthly credit bundle (1M credits/mo) — list price $36,000/mo
- Commit 12m — 6M monthly baseline: 12-month term, 15% off list for commit >= 6M/mo (annualized). Includes 100k one-time onboarding credits.

Notes on discounts and flexibility:
- Standard committed-term discounts range 10–18% depending on term length and dollar commitment. We can layer a limited onboarding credit or professional services discount for pilots converting to committed annuals.
- For short latency SLOs, we recommend preserving a low-latency model variant in the routing policy and using Optimize credits to subsidize background/regeneration workloads; this preserves p95 while reducing overall unit cost.

Practical example (your 6M tokens/month pilot):
- Baseline (no optimize): estimated $X per token (see attached for per scenario math).
- With batching + cache + int8 quant: estimated 45–55% reduction in per-token compute cost (combined effect). Int4 could push to ~60% in lab conditions but expect 1–2% hit in some ranking cases without per-prompt eval.

Attachments: Optimize_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (breakdown by band + model/seq length assumptions).

Next steps: I can loop Ben (sales) and Karthik (inference) onto a 30-minute call to agree a MAP and finalize a preferred commercial band. Does tomorrow afternoon (June 19) at 2pm PT work for you?

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
[Attachment: Optimize_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: ACME-4721 — proposed concession range

Irene — quick internal.

Acme looks solid but procurement will push for max concessions. I'm OK to authorize a 15% committed-term discount on the 12m band (for >=6M/mo baseline) but want to attach a one-time onboarding credit no larger than $20k to preserve margin. Alternative: 12% + $25k PS credit if they need more hands-on help.

Notes / ask: can we confirm (Karthik) that the technical recommendations (int8 + caching) are implementable within their latency SLO without product changes? If yes, I'll present the 15% + $15k onboarding credit as our commercial offer.

If product can't guarantee p95 on dev traffic without variant routing, we should prefer 12% + higher onboarding credit to cover engineering support.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Helen Carter <helen.carter@acmeretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Liu <alex.liu@acmeretail.com>, procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2027-06-20T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — packaging, quantization & credits

Irene / Ben — thanks for the clear options. After discussing with procurement, we're prepared to move forward on the following commercial terms: 

- 15% off list on a 12-month committed band (baseline 6M tokens/month)
- One-time onboarding credit: $15,000 applied at contract signature
- MAP with milestones: pilot (30 days), performance validation (60 days), Prod rollout (90 days). Please send a 1-page MAP and a DocuSign-ready order form for legal/procurement.

Procurement contact: procurement@acmeretail.com (cc'd) — I've also attached their standard procurement packet.

On the tech side, we'll run the int8 path initially and evaluate int4 on a focused evaluation set. We accept the caveat on a small quality delta and will run the Redwood-provided eval harness.

Thanks — Helen
[Attachment: Acme_Req_Procurement.pdf (pdf)]
